A pie chart showing the ideal composition of a loam soil. Mineral matter takes up nearly half the circle (45%, shaded brown), water (25%, shaded blue) and air (25%, shaded light grey) each take up a quarter, and organic matter takes up a small slice (5%, shaded green). Labels must clearly state the percentages. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A cross-section diagram of a mature soil profile showing five distinct horizontal layers. Top layer (O horizon): thin, dark, covered in leaf litter and grass. Second layer (A horizon): thicker, dark brown topsoil with plant roots. Third layer (B horizon): lighter reddish-brown subsoil with accumulated clay and deep roots. Fourth layer (C horizon): yellowish-grey layer filled with large chunks of weathered rock. Bottom layer (R horizon): solid, unbroken grey bedrock. Labels must point to each horizon: "O horizon (Organic)", "A horizon (Topsoil / Zone of Eluviation)", "B horizon (Subsoil / Zone of Illuviation)", "C horizon (Weathered parent rock)", "R or D horizon (Bedrock)".
